cutoverUnits.description: Request timing, protected context, headers, rules, classification, deduplication, and resource-state handoff.
Document-start Worker, fetch, XHR, JSON, TextDecoder, key, manifest, and page-action runtime bundle.
MediaSource capture, bounded page buffering, main spool, reset, finalize, and merge lifecycle.
HLS parse, plan, key, map, range, rendition, live, retry, preprocessing, and byte-output semantics.
DASH parse, plan, BaseURL, timeline, track, range, download, merge, and rejection semantics.
Concurrent transfer, Range, retry, abort, ordered output, cancellation, memory budget, and task ownership.
Verified staged output, leases, ffmpeg, local save, library delivery, normal downloads, external tools, and workflow projection.

capabilities.notes: Seed gap: the current bridge records onCompleted rather than first byte and has no explicit cancellation/redirect closure contract. Local closure remains incomplete.
Seed gap: sensitive header values cross main, preload, renderer, plans, tools, and download commands; the current Map has no TTL or capacity budget.
Seed only: Cat Catch request-header and URL filtering helpers are now anchored to the observed upstream bytes, but their dependency closure and OmniFlow mapping have not been audited.
Seed mapping only; ordering and heuristic parity have not been proven against the pinned upstream closure.
The current main Map is the production state owner but has no entry budget, TTL, or application-wide disposal method.
Seed gap: resource and processing DTOs are duplicated across main, preload, ambient declarations, renderer types, and APIs.
Explicit tab close is the strongest current cleanup path; navigation, render-process-gone, spontaneous destruction, and app exit leave different owner subsets behind.

upstreamSources.anchor: Worker fetch XHR JSON TextDecoder hooks

capabilities.notes: Known seed gap: enableDeepRuntimeHooks is hard-coded false; Worker/fetch/XHR/JSON/key hooks are inactive, TextDecoder is absent, and JSON limits differ from upstream.
Current heuristics exist but no complete upstream behavior map or differential evidence is recorded.
Seed security gap: the console-prefix envelope has no nonce or capability validation, so an untrusted page can forge resource and MSE events.
The eight current toolkit preferences are persisted in each visited site's origin localStorage, not in an application-level owner; capture enabled state itself is memory-only.
MSE is the only currently active runtime hook family; parity, bounded page retention, and append/endOfStream observability are unverified.
Spool files and write queues are controller Maps with no global budget, reaper, quarantine, crash recovery, or app-exit closure.

upstreamSources.anchor: HLS manifest parsing and plan construction

capabilities.notes: The renderer currently owns parser/planner semantics and sends a complete plan to main; hidden BYTERANGE offsets and full upstream closure remain unverified.
No single task/cancel owner spans plan execution, retry sessions, work directories, and renderer listeners.
Live recorders are held in a controller Map; close-tab attempts cleanup but app exit and crash recovery do not share the same closure.

upstreamSources.anchor: PNG and JPEG disguised fragment preprocessing

capabilities.notes: Known unmapped gap: one-shot manifest cache fallback and PNG/JPEG disguised-fragment preprocessing are not present in the local production path.
The current hand-written renderer parser is not supported by a mature parser oracle or complete specification fixtures.
Known seed gap includes SegmentTimeline r=-1 and incomplete dynamic MPD semantics; main trusts the renderer-supplied plan.
Local AbortControllers exist inside the downloader, but the orchestration layer does not retain a uniform cancel handle or terminal task record.
Known gap: direct downloads and selected HTTP/resource reads materialize complete responses in memory.
There is no application-wide task registry; task truth is split across controller Maps, child operations, component refs, hooks, and promises.
Current processing reports success with a raw outputPath before local-save or UploadManager delivery reaches a terminal state.
Raw paths and temporary directories are held by renderer workflows; no opaque lease, TTL, owner task, reaper, or quarantine exists.
Feature component unmount currently loses the task projection and listener ownership; no application-scoped recovery projection exists.
UploadManager is the upload task owner, but the current embedded-browser workflow awaits creation flow rather than maintaining a durable processing/delivery association.
Seed only: filename filtering, template evaluation, large-buffer conversion, and direct data-URL output are anchored, but helper consumers and output semantics remain unmapped.

The current main-process file-save service copies or writes extracted resource bytes to a user-selected path, but delivery terminal state and staged-output release are not yet owned by the planned adapter.
Normal BrowserWindow download completion and optional library import form a separate handoff from captured-output local save and retain their own cleanup lifecycle.
ffmpeg child processes are created by multiple services and are not registered under a common task/cancel/app-exit owner.
The current main dispatcher consumes renderer-supplied URL and header payloads and spawns external processes without the planned protected-context capability boundary.
